THVD1452DR and THVD1450DR put A and B in separate packages. The datasheet states a 40 ns maximum receiver delay and no minimum, so the skew between the A and B receivers is bounded only by 40 ns. At 5 MHz the quadrature edge spacing is 50 ns, so the worst-case spacing at the RP2354B is 50 - 40 = 10 ns. P2's quad_edge cycle model decodes down to 14 ns and fails at 13 ns. On that model the two parts hold decoding up to 1 / (4 x (14 + 40) ns) = 4.63 MHz a channel, and at 1 MHz single-ended (250 ns spacing). AM26LV32EIDR, with A and B in one package, has 6 ns maximum output skew (tsk(o)), leaving 44 ns. Derived from datasheet limits and P2's model; not measured
